title: COMPUTING MACHINERY 2
body:
The sequel to [[COMPUTING MACHINERY]], and it goes in two directions at once. Downward into
the gates: how a [[CPU]] is built out of [[Combinational Logic]] and [[Sequential Logic]],
and why a circuit with feedback has memory. Outward into the world: how a processor talks to
a keyboard, a screen, and a sound chip, and the three escalating answers to "how do I know
the device is ready?": [[Polling]], [[Interrupts]], and [[Direct Memory Access]].

That second half is the direct prerequisite for [[OPERATING SYSTEMS]]. [[Context Switching]],
[[Concurrency]], and [[Buffering]] are introduced here as hardware facts and reappear there
as scheduling and [[Synchronization]] problems.

## Topics

### Digital logic

[[Digital Logic]] · [[Boolean Algebra]] · [[Complete Set of Operations]] · [[Digital circuit]]

[[Boolean Algebra]] is the algebra circuits are designed in. A [[Complete Set of Operations]]
is one that can express *any* boolean expression. `{NAND}` alone is complete, which is why
real hardware is built out of so many NAND gates.

### Combinational circuits

[[Combinational Logic]] · [[ALU]] · [[ROM]] · [[Multiplexer]] · [[Encoder]] ·
[[Priority Encoder]] · [[Decoder]] · [[adder-subtractor]]

No memory, no feedback: the output is a function of the current inputs and nothing else.
The [[ALU]] from [[COMPUTING MACHINERY]] is one of these.

### Sequential circuits

[[Sequential Logic]] · [[Bi-stable elements]] · [[metastability]] · [[SR-Latch]] ·
[[D-Latch]] · [[Flip-Flop]] · [[Shift Register]] · [[Characteristic Table]] ·
[[Excitation Table]] · [[Finite State Machine]] · [[Synchronous]] · [[Asynchronous]]

Feedback to the input means state, and state means memory. A [[Characteristic Table]] reads
forward (given the current state and inputs, what is the next state); an [[Excitation Table]]
reads backward (to get this transition, what inputs are needed). [[metastability]] is what
happens when a bi-stable element is caught between its two stable values.

Formally these are [[Finite State Machine]]s, the same object studied abstractly in
[[INTRODUCTION TO COMPUTABILITY]] as [[Finite Automata]].

### Analog and digital

[[Analog]] · [[Digital]] · [[Continuous]] · [[Discrete]] · [[Voltage]] · [[Current]] ·
[[DAC's and ADC's]]

[[Analog]] signals vary smoothly over a [[Continuous]] range; [[Digital]] signals take
[[Discrete]] values. Converters bridge the two, which is what makes sound possible.

### Sound

[[Sound]] · [[PCM]] · [[Sound Cards]] · [[PSG]] · [[Frequency]] · [[Amplitude]] ·
[[Sample Rate]] · [[Fidelity]] · [[YM2149]]

Sampling a continuous waveform into discrete values is [[PCM]]. Raise the [[Sample Rate]]
and you raise the [[Fidelity]], the resemblance to the real signal.

### Graphics

[[Raster Graphics]] · [[Double Buffering]] · [[VBL ISR]]

Drawing straight into the frame buffer while the screen is being scanned tears the image.
[[Double Buffering]] draws into an off-screen buffer and swaps, and the swap is driven by the
vertical-blank interrupt, the [[VBL ISR]].

### I/O structure

[[I-O]] · [[I-O Device]] · [[I-O Interface]] · [[I-O Interface Functions]] ·
[[Data Register]] · [[Status Register]] · [[Control Register]] · [[Buffering]] ·
[[Memory Mapping]] · [[Isolated I-O]] · [[System Bus]] · [[System Controller]] · [[GLUE]]

An [[I-O Interface]] is a digital circuit sitting between a device and the bus, exposing
three registers: [[Data Register]], [[Status Register]], [[Control Register]]. It exists
because devices and CPUs disagree about speed, data format, and electrical levels, hence
[[Buffering]].

[[Memory Mapping]] gives device registers ordinary memory addresses (simpler CPU, simpler
programming, at the cost of address space); [[Isolated I-O]] gives them a separate space and
separate instructions.

### Serial and parallel

[[Serial I-O]] · [[Parallel I-O]] · [[UART]] · [[6850 ACIA]] · [[Baud Rate]] ·
[[Asynchronous Handshaking]] · [[Shift Register]]

Serial moves one bit at a time through a [[Shift Register]]; parallel moves a whole word and
coordinates with [[Asynchronous Handshaking]]. The keyboard connection is serial.

### The three approaches to I/O

[[Programmed I-O]] · [[Polling]] · [[overrun]] · [[Interrupts]] ·
[[Interrupt Driven I-O]] · [[Direct Memory Access]]

| Approach | How it works | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| [[Programmed I-O]] / [[Polling]] | Loop, checking the status register | Burns the CPU; miss the window and you get an [[overrun]] |
| [[Interrupt Driven I-O]] | Device raises an [[IRQs\|IRQ]]; CPU runs an [[ISRs\|ISR]] | Needs [[Vector Tables]], [[Context Switching]], and care about [[Concurrency]] |
| [[Direct Memory Access]] | Device moves the data itself | Fastest; the CPU is only told when it's done |

### Interrupts

[[Interrupts]] · [[IRQs]] · [[ISRs]] · [[Vector Tables]] · [[IPL]] · [[Interrupt Mask]] ·
[[PIC]] · [[68901 MFP]] · [[Priority Encoder]] · [[RDR]] · [[Context Switching]] ·
[[Concurrency]] · [[Trace Bit]] · [[Supervisor State]]

An interrupt is a hardware-forced detour in the [[Fetch-Execute Cycle]]. The [[PIC]] uses a
[[Priority Encoder]] to decide which pending request wins, the [[Vector Tables]] say which
[[ISRs|ISR]] to jump to, and the ISR saves and restores context exactly like a subroutine,
because as far as the interrupted program is concerned, nothing happened.

### Keyboard and CPU internals

[[IKBD Systems]] · [[Scan Matrix]] · [[Make-Break Codes]] ·
[[CPU Organization and operation]] · [[Fetch-Execute Cycle]] · [[Motorola 68000]]

## Core Facts to Know

- A [[Combinational Logic|combinational]] circuit has no memory: the output depends only on the current inputs.
- A [[Sequential Logic|sequential]] circuit has feedback to its input, therefore state, therefore memory.
- `{NAND}` is a [[Complete Set of Operations]]: every boolean expression can be built from NAND alone.
- A [[Characteristic Table]] gives the next state from the current state and inputs.
- An [[Excitation Table]] gives the inputs needed to produce a wanted transition.
- A [[Flip-Flop]] is edge-triggered; a [[D-Latch]] is level-triggered.
- A [[Shift Register]] is a chain of cascading [[Flip-Flop]]s.
- [[metastability]] is a bi-stable element stuck between its two stable states.
- [[Analog]] means [[Continuous]]; [[Digital]] means [[Discrete]].
- [[Baud Rate]] is signal changes per second, a *signalling* rate, not a data rate.
- [[UART]] stands for Universal Asynchronous Receiver / Transmitter.
- The [[6850 ACIA]] is the 68000's UART, used for the keyboard.
- Synchronous serial always sends; asynchronous serial only sends when there is data.
- An [[I-O Interface]] exposes a [[Data Register]], a [[Status Register]], and a [[Control Register]].
- Devices need [[Buffering]] because of differences in speed, data format, and electronics.
- Memory-mapped I/O costs you address space but simplifies both the CPU and the programmer's life.
- [[Isolated I-O]] keeps device addresses in their own space, separate from memory.
- [[Polling]] is another name for [[Programmed I-O]], a busy wait on the status register.
- Polling can miss data: that's an [[overrun]].
- [[IPL]] stands for Interrupt Priority Level.
- [[RDR]] stands for Read Data Register.
- [[PIC]] stands for Programmable Interrupt Controller; the [[68901 MFP]] is the 68000's.
- The [[PIC]] uses a [[Priority Encoder]] to decide which interrupt is serviced.
- A [[Vector Tables|vector table]] is a table of [[Pointer]]s to [[ISRs]].
- An [[ISRs|ISR]] takes no parameters and returns nothing, because nobody calls it.
- An ISR must save and restore context (`movem.l d0-d2/a0-a2,-(sp)` … `movem.l (sp)+,…`).
- ISRs communicate with the main program through globals, typically a circular [[Queue]].
- Common IRQ sources: keyboard, mouse movement, and the vertical blank.
- The [[VBL ISR]] fires once per screen refresh and is where the [[Double Buffering]] swap happens.
- [[Direct Memory Access]] lets a device write to memory without the CPU moving each byte.
- Keyboards detect keypresses with a [[Scan Matrix]].
- A *make* code is the key going down; a *break* code is the key coming up.
- A scan code $S$ satisfies $0 \leq S \leq 127$.
- Increasing the [[Sample Rate]] increases [[Fidelity]].
- The [[Status Register]] holds the [[Trace Bit]], the [[Interrupt Mask]], and the [[Supervisor State]] bit.

## Related courses

- [[COMPUTING MACHINERY]], the prequel: [[Motorola 68000]], [[CPU]], [[Assembly]],
  [[Addressing Modes]], [[Status Bits]], and the support chips this course wires up.
- [[OPERATING SYSTEMS]]: takes [[Context Switching]], [[Concurrency]], [[Buffering]], and
  [[Interrupts]] and turns them into [[Processes]], [[CPU Scheduling]], and
  [[Synchronization]]. [[Polling]] here is the same busy-wait argument as a [[Spin Lock]] there.
- [[INTRODUCTION TO COMPUTABILITY]]: [[Finite State Machine]]s built out of flip-flops are
  [[Finite Automata]] studied as mathematics.
- [[INFORMATION STRUCTURES]]: the circular [[Queue]] an [[ISRs|ISR]] writes into.
- [[INTRODUCTION TO COMPUTER SCIENCE 2]]: [[Pointer]]s, which is all a vector table is.
